_readme: THE HAULOVER GATE -- a playable scene. You are at the helm of the Novurania 18 RHIB in the
Merrimack entrance on the afternoon ebb of 2026-08-28, at sunset. Ahead, across the channel, stands a
gate: a 120 m x 30 m x 10 m box, and a window -- through it, faintly outlined, is Haulover's sea.
Drive your boat into it and you come out of Baker's Haulover Inlet, Miami, heading out to sea,
still moving. The box is one motor between two places on the same planet: nothing else moves.
200 m on, at Haulover, stands a second gate: the way back. It comes out here, 200 m short of the
first -- so the first window shows the second, which shows this inlet again with the first gate
in it, and so on: windows within windows, each one a real place seen through glass. Keep
driving and you go round.
Launch from the repo root:  build/bin/gagame.exe scenes/demos/haulover_portal.json
HELM   W / S  both throttles ahead / astern      A / D  steer to port / starboard
Q / E  split the levers (pivot)           Shift / Ctrl  trim out / in
T      leave the helm: the camera flies free (the boat keeps its throttles); T again returns
FLY    W A S D move, Q / E down / up, hold the right mouse button to look, wheel = speed
TIME   Space pause, Up / Down time x10 / /10, Left / Right nudge.   R reload shaders.
Haulover's own terrain is in the tree: NOAA's ninth-arc-second CUDEM tiles (FL n26X00 and n26X25,
w080X25; NAVD88 metres), harvested 2026-09-28 (data/places/haulover.json), are named below as a
height source by their files and folded onto the pyramid at first boot (about ten seconds). What
the renderer READS at Haulover today is the cube's level of that fold (611 m texels): the finer
levels wait for the blocks path (HIERARCHY 4.17) to stand there, so the inlet's shape is coarse
and the water is open sea. The Merrimack is as it is in the other demos.
2026-09-30: runs on the residency manager of HIERARCHY 4.19 with a 2 GB pool, every read
addressed about the eye (4.4), and the land as its imagery (the painted rock is out).

sun._readme: The sun is a light at 0,0,0 and the Earth is placed around it -- no clock involved, so the tide above keeps its own time. This placement puts the Merrimack at sunset (+1.5 deg) and Haulover in daylight (+20.0 deg): the sun lies along the great circle from one inlet through the other.
